top_categories.workout_context: Gran Fondo Maryland's brutally hilly forested mountain roads forces constant power changes. Accelerate over rises and out of corners, settle on the open road, and repeat for 87 miles.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Gran Fondo Maryland's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before September.
98ft/mi means long efforts at or near FTP on every climb. If your threshold cracks at minute 15, you'll walk the rest.
At Gran Fondo Maryland, surges push you above threshold and you have to recover while still riding. Over-unders train exactly that.
8,500ft of climbing means repeated surges above threshold. VO2max work is how you survive the fifth climb, not just the first.
At mile 60 of 87, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Gran Fondo Maryland. Train it until it feels boring.
How long can you hold 105% FTP before you blow? At Gran Fondo Maryland, that number decides whether you bridge or get dropped.
8,500ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
Short, max efforts are unavoidable. Punchy climbs, gap closures, attacks on brutally hilly forested mountain roads. If you haven't trained them, you'll crack.
Low-cadence force work for 8,500ft of climbing. The slow, grinding ascents where you can't spin—you push.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 8,500ft of climbing on brutally hilly forested mountain roads does to your power file on race day.

race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Gran Fondo Maryland’s 87 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.altitude: Moderate altitude at Gran Fondo Maryland. Arrive 2–3 days early. Reduce intensity expectations by 5–10%. Hydrate aggressively.
race_overlay.terrain: Highly technical terrain at Gran Fondo Maryland demands practice on similar surfaces. Ride brutally hilly forested mountain roads at race-day cadence weekly. Practice cornering, descending, and power delivery on unstable surfaces. Test tires and pressure in comparable conditions before race week rather than guessing from a generic time-loss claim.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Road Specific, Race Simulation, and TT Threshold to prepare you for 87 miles of brutally hilly forested mountain roads in Frederick, Maryland, USA.
